newsitem.title: USA: Enviromentalists seek SEC look into Viacom.
newsitem.headline: Enviromentalists seek SEC look into Viacom.

text.p: Three environmental groups said Monday they requested a regulatory agency investigate Viacom Inc's failure to disclose a potential liability for $300 million in cleanup costs in its 1995 annual report.

In a Feb 26 letter to Securites and Exchange Commission, Friends of the Earth, Citizen Action and Sierra Club wrote that Viacom and its subsidiaries are potentially financially responsible at more than 30 state or federal superfund sites.
Viacom disputed this claim saying in a statement the letter is "misleading and inaccurate."
"We are confident we've assessed our environmental liabilities reasonably and that they are fully and fairly reflected in our financial statements and our 10-K," it said.
In the letter, the groups say Viacom is the sole or major party responsible for clean-up at six superfund sites where remediation and clean-ups costs are estimated at $270 million.

Viacom's share of the other 24 sites is less clear cut because it shares responsibility with other parties, the groups said. But even if its share is just five percent, the total potential liabilty could reach $300 million.
Viacom said the environmentalists overstated the estimates of the liabilities and the $270 million cost attributed to the six sites "bears no relation to reality."
Viacom and its predecessors have "responsibly spent tens of millions of dollars on cleanup efforts, principally related to the operations of Gulf & Western," the company said.
SEC policy prohibits it from commenting on any correspondence received including confirming whether it actually received the letter.
In 1994, Viacom merged with Paramount, which was formerly known as Gulf & Western.
